judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant turns on policies written 'to apply excess of underlying insurance which afford limits not less than' the scheduled limits, and 'underlying insurance' is genuinely contestable — it may or may not embrace a self-insured retention, and 'not less than the limits specified' leaves the consequence of a shortfall unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article III (c012/c056/c076) expressly contemplates that the underlying Hospital Professional Liability limit may be 'self-insured', which sits awkwardly with Article I's requirement of underlying 'insurance', and Amendment No. 4 (c070) replaces this paragraph only for policies effective on or after October 1, 1996, leaving two application clauses running in parallel.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A schedule of figures with defined trigger terms ('each occurrence', 'each medical incident', 'combined single limit'); the numbers are definite even if the transcription is poor.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendment No. 4 (c071) adds overlapping and partly duplicative entries for Nursing Homes/Outpatient Facilities, and Article III's self-insured proviso assumes underlying limits that need not be insured at all.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Subject to the provision that a separate limit of liability may apply in respect thereof' is permissive and unattributed — it does not say whose limit, whose option, or when a separate limit applies.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article XI (c033) separately preserves discovery-period and extended-reporting coverages after cancellation, and Rating Schedule-B's claim-conversion note (c086) promises a free extended reporting endorsement, so the treatment of these extensions is spread across three provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare incorporation sentence with nothing to construe on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It pulls in the Insolvency Clause (c046), whose 'amount of liability' payment basis stands in tension with Article IV's 'actually paid' definition of loss, but the incorporating sentence itself does not create that tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Teaching hospital', 'children's hospital' and 'psychiatric hospital' are undefined institutional categories, and 'loss arising out of the operation by the insured of' such a hospital is a broad causal phrase whose reach over a multi-site system is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendment No. 1 (c053) deletes this exclusion for policies effective on or after July 1, 1995 and narrows it to teaching hospitals only, so both versions operate on different tranches of business at once.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical definition mixes 'occupied acute care beds' with 'all' bassinets, psychiatric, alcohol/drug, rehabilitation and long-term beds, so whether the 250-bed count is of occupied or licensed beds is genuinely unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendment No. 1 (c054) substitutes a 350-bed threshold using the identical definition, and the Rating Schedules count 'occupied' beds only, which pulls against counting 'all' beds here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Arising out of the ownership, operation or use of helicopters owned or leased by the insured hospital' is a standard formulation; its terms are reasonably definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article I (c001) affirmatively lists 'Heliport Liability' among the covered coverages while this exclusion strips out helicopter-related loss for owned or leased aircraft, leaving the covered heliport exposure hard to identify.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of named counties; nothing vague in it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendment No. 1 (c055) deletes Cuyahoga and adds Wayne and Oakland Counties, and the Rating Schedules then price Cleveland (Cuyahoga) as Territory 3, so the exclusion's scope changes date-by-date.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enumerated 'pool, syndicate, association, insolvency fund, guaranty fund' is followed by the catch-all 'or other combination of insurers or reinsurers formed for the purpose of...', a textbook ejusdem generis problem about how far the catch-all reaches.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nuclear Incident Exclusion Clause No. 1(1) (c034) and No. 2(1) (c043) exclude pool liability again in narrower terms, which is duplicative rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reinsurance assumed by the REINSURED' is a short, well-understood market term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Article I's grant, which reaches only the REINSURED's own excess liability policies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Business to the extent that it is reinsured outside of this agreement' is open-ended: it does not say whether it means other reinsurance of the same layer, any other reinsurance, or facultative placements, and 'to the extent' invites proportional argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against Article III's promise to indemnify '100% of such loss' and the Offset article (c032) which contemplates other reinsurance agreements between the same parties, so the interaction with other covers is not worked out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The retention formula is dense and contains an internal numerical mismatch ('$9,000,000 of loss each occurrence/$93,000,000 annual aggregate' against $10,000,000 limits), which is the kind of writing error that changes meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This article is deleted and replaced twice (c056 by Amendment No. 1 and c076 by Amendment No. 4), so limits of $10,000,000 and $25,000,000 coexist across the instrument depending on policy date.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Loss' is confined to amounts 'actually paid by the REINSURED' within 'applicable policy limits', with 90% carve-outs for extra-contractual and punitive amounts conditioned on the CORPORATION having 'counseled with' and 'concurred in' the REINSURED's conduct — every one of those phrases is a live definitional battleground.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 'actually paid' limitation is squarely in tension with the Insolvency Clause (c046), which requires payment 'on the basis of the amount of liability of the ceding insurer ... without diminution', and with Article IX's advance-funding sentence (c030) requiring payment before the REINSURED pays.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Net salvage, subrogation or any other recovery (after expenses)' contains a catch-all but the reduction mechanic it states is arithmetically definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Accounting Schedule (c021) credits 'all salvage received by the CORPORATION' to profits, which is consistent with this recovery-sharing rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition ties 'claim expenses' to 'all payments under the supplementary payments provisions of the REINSURED'S policy' and then adds an 'including' list, so it is unclear whether expenses not falling under a supplementary payments provision (or incurred under an excess policy with no duty to defend) are captured at all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interlocks with Article V's pro rata indemnity (c017), Article IV's exclusion of salaries and statutory penalties (c016) and Article IX's allocation of defense to the REINSURED (c027), and whether such expenses fall inside or outside the Article III limits is nowhere stated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short, concrete carve-outs; 'salaries paid to employees' and 'statutory penalty' are reasonably determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the definitions in c013 and c015; it narrows both without contradicting either.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The pro rata formula ('that proportion ... that the amount of loss ultimately borne by the CORPORATION bears to the total amount of loss') breaks down where there is no loss or where loss exceeds the limits, and the appeal proviso speaks of 'such settlement or appeal' when no settlement was previously mentioned.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing in Article III (c012/c056/c076) says whether this expense indemnity is inside or in addition to the '$25,000,000 each occurrence' limit, and Article IX (c028) makes the CORPORATION's own participation 'at its own expense', which cuts across the sharing formula here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A straightforward premium obligation keyed to an attached schedule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'The Rating Schedule, attached hereto' is deleted and replaced by Schedule-A (c057) and then Schedule-B (c077), so the referent shifts over time although the substitution clauses say so expressly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single percentage figure with a named payee; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Accounting Schedule (c021) credits premium 'net after ceding commission', which dovetails with this clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The accounting-period mechanics are internally odd: periods run twenty-four months from every other January 1, yet on off-cycle termination the final period is said to commence on 'the fifth January 1st preceding the termination date', which cannot be reconciled with a two-year period.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendment No. 1 (c052) deletes only the first paragraph of this article and substitutes a formula capped at 'the first $1,000,000 of reinsured limits', leaving these timing mechanics and the Accounting Schedule (c021) to operate on a differently-scoped commission.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The credit and charge items are enumerated with figures, but the items are garbled and the charge for 'claims occurring or claims made (depending on policy coverage) during the accounting period' leaves period-attribution for claims-made business unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Schedule provides no method for allocating premium, losses and the 15% overhead charge to the 'first $1,000,000 of reinsured limits' layer to which Amendment No. 1 (c052) confines the contingent commission, which is a genuine gap in the amended scheme.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Calculated on the reserve of individual cases as developed to the date the computation is made' does not say whose reserve controls — the REINSURED's or the CORPORATION's — which drives the whole commission calculation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Accounting Schedule (c021) charges 'unpaid losses' to profits and Article X (c031) gives only an inspection right, so no provision resolves who sets the case reserves.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definitional sentence with a clear carry-forward mechanic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It meshes with item 4 of the charges in the Accounting Schedule (c021) and the net profit definition (c024).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The excess of credits over charges' is arithmetically definite given the Accounting Schedule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendment No. 1 (c052) speaks of 'net profit accruing to the REINSURED under this agreement' limited to the first $1,000,000 of reinsured limits, a scope this whole-agreement definition does not accommodate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is mangled but its two limbs — no accounting period commencing on or after termination, and no further commission until all premium is earned and all losses paid — are themselves in tension with periodic annual computation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article VII's own deferral mechanics (c020) contemplate computations continuing for years after a period closes, and the run-off provisions in Article XI (c033) and the Stipulation of Termination (c099) keep liabilities open long after termination.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two concrete 20-day deadlines; 'a form satisfactory to the CORPORATION' is discretionary but administrative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing in Articles VI, VII or IX contradicts the monthly bordereau and remittance cycle.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Prompt notice ... of any event or development which might result in a claim' is a low, vague threshold, and the consequence of late notice is unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Insolvency Clause (c047) repeats the duty to investigate, settle and defend and adds a 'reasonable time' notice standard for the liquidator, a different formulation of the same obligation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The right to participate is triggered by claims to which 'in the judgment of the CORPORATION, it is or might become exposed' — a wholly subjective and unbounded trigger — and 'participate jointly' is not defined against the REINSURED's exclusive control of the defense.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'At its own expense' here cuts against Article V (c017), which makes the CORPORATION share claim expenses pro rata, and against Article IX's first paragraph (c027), which commits investigation, settlement and defense to the REINSURED alone.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Promptly' and 'satisfactory evidence of payment' are both elastic, and the clause conditions reimbursement on payment having already been made.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The very next paragraph (c030) requires the CORPORATION to fund on the date the REINSURED proposes to pay, and the Insolvency Clause (c046) requires payment without diminution regardless of actual payment, so three provisions state different payment triggers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is garbled and its operative promise — to 'furnish ... the CORPORATION'S payment of loss' on the date the REINSURED proposes to pay — is imprecise about what advance notice suffices and what happens if the REINSURED does not then pay.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reverses the condition in the immediately preceding paragraph (c029), which makes reimbursement contingent on evidence that loss has already been paid, and it interacts with the 'actually paid' definition of loss in Article IV (c013).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence access right; 'pertaining to the risks reinsured hereunder' is a mild but ordinary limitation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other article limits or enlarges the inspection right; it coexists with the reporting duty in Article VIII (c026).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any balance, whether on account of premiums, commissions, loss or claim expenses' is a broad but conventionally drafted offset right.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Offset in insolvency is a familiar flashpoint against the Insolvency Clause (c046), which requires payment to the liquidator without diminution, and the reach across 'any other reinsurance agreement' overlaps exclusion (g) (c011).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'In no event exceeding 12 months plus odd time' uses an undefined trade phrase, and 'in force prior to or as of the effective date in time of cancellation' is garbled enough to obscure which extended reporting endorsements are preserved.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Stipulation of Termination (c099) terminates the agreement by reference to policies 'issued on or after January 1, 1998' rather than by the 90-day notice and run-off mechanic set out here, so the two termination routes do not align.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, standard market exclusion for pool-derived nuclear liability.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates part of Article II(e) (c009) without contradicting it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enumerated installations end with a residual category using 'substantial quantities of radioactive isotopes', an undefined quantitative standard within an otherwise specific list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere in the agreement addresses nuclear physical damage exposure, so there is little to conflict with.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exception turns on whether the REINSURED 'does not have knowledge' of the nuclear installation and on approval by 'the Governmental Authority', both of which are indeterminate as drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It operates only within the nuclear clause and does not engage the operative articles of the agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A named hazard specifically insured against' is a reasonably settled insurance formulation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Self-contained within the nuclear exclusion; no other provision addresses named-peril radioactive contamination.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It excepts risks where the nuclear exposure 'is not considered by the REINSURED to be the primary hazard' — a purely subjective test — and carries over the undefined 'substantial quantities'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has no counterpart elsewhere in the agreement to contradict, though it sits oddly with the CORPORATION's inspection and judgment rights in Articles IX and X.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition by statutory reference to the Atomic Energy Act; externally fixed and determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the instrument defines 'special nuclear material'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Making the REINSURED 'sole judge' of 'substantial quantities' and 'the extent of installation, plant or site' hands one party unilateral definitional power over vague terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts against the CORPORATION's inspection right (c031) and its judgment-based participation right (c028), but only within the nuclear exclusion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A dated grandfathering rule whose expiry date is garbled in transcription but which is mechanical in substance.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 1957 date long predates the January 1, 1994 effective date in Article I, so the provision is inert rather than conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same dated grandfathering structure for Canadian risks; mechanical and time-barred.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Inert against an agreement effective in 1994 and applying to Ohio-area hospital risks.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short association-membership exclusion in standard form.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It substantially overlaps Article II(e) (c009) and Nuclear Clause No. 1(1) (c034), a redundancy rather than a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The deemed Limited Exclusion Provision applies to enumerated personal-lines forms 'or policies of a similar nature', a general tail on a specific list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The enumerated personal auto and homeowners forms bear no relation to the hospital excess liability business described in Article I, so the clause is largely inapplicable rather than inconsistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Broad Exclusion Provision is deemed into a specific list of commercial liability coverages, and the boundary of that list against the coverages actually reinsured is not stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article I (c001) reinsures Hospital Professional and other liability coverages that overlap this list, so the deemed exclusion reaches business the agreement otherwise covers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause carves out 'except as provided by Section 4118 of the Insurance Law of New York' in an agreement between Kansas and Ohio companies, an incongruous reference, and the judgment-evidence sentences are dense.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its 'amount of liability ... without diminution' payment basis stands directly against Article IV's definition of loss as amounts 'actually paid by the REINSURED' (c013), a tension the Article IV proviso only partly resolves.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Within a reasonable time' and 'a proportionate share of the benefit which may accrue' are elastic, but the structure of the duty is conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restates the Article IX duty to investigate, settle and defend (c027) in different words and gives the reinsurer a defense right at its own expense that parallels but does not match Article IX's participation right (c028).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A majority in interest' among reinsurers is undefined, and expenses are to be apportioned 'in accordance with the terms of this reinsurance agreement' which contains no multi-reinsurer apportionment rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article V (c017) supplies only a two-party pro rata formula, so the referenced apportionment terms do not exist in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A savings clause with double negatives and nested 'except as hereinabove specifically provided' qualifiers, but its purpose is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It declares that nothing enlarges either party's obligations while the same clause changes the payment basis on insolvency, and it must be read with Article IV's 'loss' definition (c013).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The bed-equivalent factors are numeric, but 'CRNAs - each full-time equivalent x 5-10' states a range rather than a rate, leaving the multiplier indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This schedule is deleted in its entirety by Amendment No. 1 (c057) and replaced by Schedule-A and then Schedule-B, which carry the identical unresolved 5-10 range.
